office_explainer: Writes and votes on federal laws and the federal budget. Serves a two-year term.

candidates.background: Has represented Maryland's 2nd District in Congress since 2025 (Maryland Matters). Grew up in eastern Baltimore County.

own_words.text: On elections: "I also oppose legislation that creates new barriers to voting like the SAVE Act."
On immigration enforcement: "I do not" support current approaches; says ICE "has repeatedly undermined public trust."
On costs: says he is fighting "against the tariffs, and for the ACA tax credits."

candidates.name: Dave Wallace
candidates.background: Describes himself as "a businessman, employer, researcher, community advocate" and "not a career politician" (Maryland Matters candidate statement).

office: Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners, At Large
office_explainer: Sets city school policy, hires the schools CEO and approves the budget. Two of 11 adult seats are elected.
why_it_matters: Four candidates for two elected seats; the top two win. You may vote for up to 2. The other nine adult members are appointed by the mayor. The new board will face budget pressure, enrollment declines and likely school closures (Banner). All four are registered Democrats, from self-described moderate liberal to Democratic socialist (Banner, Oct 9).
incumbent: Ashley Ash Esposito; Kwame Jamal Kenyatta-Bey

candidates.name: Jamar Day
candidates.background: 38. Former City Schools dean of students and DC history teacher; former aide in Gov. Wes Moore's office; now at the Maryland Department of General Services. Ran partly over the closure of the Baltimore Collegiate School for Boys (Banner).

own_words.text: "I oppose vouchers and BOOST, which divert public dollars from schools."
"Safe, free transportation is necessary." Fewer high schools mean longer, riskier commutes.
In the primary, called for a pause on school closures until the board has "a clear, community-informed plan."

candidates.name: Ashley Ash Esposito
candidates.background: 42. Elected to the school board in 2022; chairs its Policy Committee. Former executive director of Baltimore Unity Hall and Baltimore Renters United; has a child in City Schools (Banner, League answers).

own_words.text: "I want equity reviews before every budget vote. Equal is not the same as fair."
"I publish plain language explanations of every vote within 72 hours."
Wants to "Protect immigrant families with a clear ICE non-cooperation policy."

candidates.name: Domonique A. Flowers
candidates.background: 42. Attorney with special education law experience and adjunct professor at the University of Baltimore; former City Schools substitute teacher; father of two (Banner).

own_words.text: Supports "policies that overhaul the current education funding system" toward historically underserved communities.
Would update standards to teach real-world skills: "financial literacy, resume writing, etc."
Would create "parent advisory councils" and focus on safety, tardiness and absenteeism.

candidates.name: Kwame Jamal Kenyatta-Bey
candidates.background: Elected school board member; City Schools and Morgan State graduate with over three decades as an educator in the system; cellist and theater director (Banner). Did not respond to The Banner's questionnaire.

own_words.text: "Maryland's schools risk prioritizing tests over learning," sidelining arts and career-technical education.
Says the Blueprint for Maryland's Future "gives us a roadmap to fix" historic underfunding.
"I support a student-centered, equitable curriculum that fosters critical thinking, hands-on learning, and multiple pathways to success."
